insight: cognitive error != hallucination; both low-accuracy; certainty (strength of belief) is the separator; harm = certainty x inaccuracy; HEM-GILE diagonal = calibration reference
model_is_illustrative_69: by-construction; shapes are the deliverable. Empirical upgrade: calibration datasets (confidence vs correctness) + self-correction/challenge probe to operationalize 'strongly believed / incorrigible' vs revisable error.

findings.separator_is_certainty: hallucination (low a, high q) and cognitive error (low a, low q) share low accuracy; only certainty distinguishes them -> certainty is the EHD-1 separator, exactly as Brandon states.
findings.harm_multiplier: mean harm hallucination 0.484 vs cognitive error 0.111 (~4.3x) -> at comparable inaccuracy, strongly-believed wrongness is far more damaging; certainty is the harm multiplier.
findings.ties_to_HAH1: hallucination here = the high-certainty/low-evidence hyper-imagining of B78 (HAH-1); EHD-1 supplies the certainty criterion that operationally separates HAH-1's 'hyper-imagining' from ordinary ERR.
findings.calibration: HEM-GILE calibration (q=a diagonal) is the reference; hallucination is the largest DANGEROUS overconfidence gap (q>>a at low a), error a small/benign gap.

principles_status: EHD-1 (Error-Hallucination Distinction) introduced CANDIDATE canonical, operational refinement/twin of HAH-1 (B78). VPP-1 EXTENDED (caps/bold/italics emphasis = intonation channel, VPP-1c) - no new count. Ratification = Brandon choice. Canonical count unchanged 74.
